32) To develop appreciation for mathematics among children, a teacher performs the following activities in the class. Choose the one which is not effective to achieve her objective.
option_a: She always praises the student who achieves highest marks in the class in the term-end examination.
option_b: She shows to children the videos on Indian mathematicians and their contributions.

question_text: 33) Which of the following statements is not correct ?
option_a: Errors of the students give information about their thought process.
option_b: Errors in mathematics are part of learning.
option_c: Errors in mathematics help teachers in planning their lessons.
option_d: Errors of the students should be overlooked as pointing errors will demotivate them.

question_text: 34) Which of the following statements is not correct about assessment ?
option_a: Norm-referenced assessment is useful in diagnostic testing and remedial teaching.
option_b: Criterion-referenced assessment is to evaluate the mastery learning of the students.
option_c: Criterion-referenced assessment is useful in diagnostic testing and remedial teaching.
option_d: Norm-referenced assessment tells us where a student stands as compared to other students in his/her performance.

question_text: 38) According to the National Curriculum Framework, 2005, classroom researches have indicated a fairly systematic devaluation of girls as incapable of mastering mathematics even when they perform well in mathematics. What is the most appropriate reason for this ?
option_a: Poor performance of girls in mathematics is due to the fear of mathematics prevalent in them.
option_b: Mathematics, by its nature, is a male-dominated subject.
option_c: Gendered constructs of society have led to the belief that boys use more innovative strategies for problem-solving and thus have better conceptual understanding.
option_d: The mathematical abilities in boys are innate.

question_text: 39) Classroom researches have shown that most of the students find mathematics more difficult than the other subjects they study in the same class. Which of the following aspects of the nature of mathematics adds to this fear ?
option_a: The vast knowledge base of mathematics
option_b: The scope of multiple answers to a given question in mathematics
option_c: The scope of a number of different methods to solve a problem in mathematics
option_d: The abstract nature of primary concepts in mathematics
